title: Bridging lender restructures £525k North London deal
summary:
Pallas Capital has provided a £525,000 bridging finance facility for the acquisition and refurbishment of a residential property in North London. The 12-month loan was restructured from a purchase bridge to a refinance facility within 10 days after third-party delays affected the completion timeline.

title: Atelier provides £12.5m for 37-home Matlock development
summary:
Atelier has provided £12.5 million in development finance to support the construction of 37 homes in Matlock, Derbyshire. The facility will fund a residential scheme comprising 26 private homes and 11 affordable dwellings over a 24-month term.

The post Atelier provides £12.5m for 37-home Matlock development appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Dutch investors secure £1.4m bridge for Bristol farmhouse
summary:
Specialist lender Glenhawk has provided £1.4 million in bridging finance to Dutch property investors acquiring a farmhouse and holiday let cottage complex in Bristol. The facility was structured at 75% loan-to-purchase-price and involved complex offshore ownership arrangements.

The post Dutch investors secure £1.4m bridge for Bristol farmhouse appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Bath council warns enforcement funding relies on fines
summary:
Bath and North East Somerset Council has raised concerns that enforcement of the Renters' Rights Act will need to be funded through fines and prosecutions of non-compliant landlords. The council indicated that sufficient funding has not necessarily been allocated to cover enforcement of the regulations.

The post Bath council warns enforcement funding relies on fines appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Former Knight Frank directors establish Midlands consultancy
summary:
Two former senior leaders from Knight Frank's land and development team have established a residential development consultancy based in Warwickshire. Will Jordan and Charlie Steele have launched Ashlawn Chase in Henley-in-Arden, bringing nearly 40 years of combined experience in the Midlands property market.

title: Winkworth removes AI-enhanced property images after complaint
summary:
Estate agency franchise Winkworth has removed AI-enhanced property photographs from a listing in Tooting, south London, following complaints that the images misrepresented the property. The incident raises questions about disclosure standards in property marketing.

The post Winkworth removes AI-enhanced property images after complaint appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Freeholder group declines to disclose funding sources
summary:
A campaign group representing freeholders has declined to reveal the identities of its financial backers, raising questions about transparency as leasehold reform debates intensify. Justice for Property Rights claims to represent over 250 members but will not disclose its funding sources.

The post Freeholder group declines to disclose funding sources appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK house prices fall 0.6% in May as Middle East uncertainty bites
summary:
UK house prices declined 0.6% in May 2026, marking the first monthly fall of the year, according to Nationwide Building Society. Annual house price growth slowed to 1.7%, down from 3.0% in April, with the average home valued at £278,024.

title: Renters’ Rights Act may increase guarantor requirements
summary:
Nearly half of England's local authority areas could require tenants to provide guarantors following the implementation of the Renters' Rights Act, according to research from Zero Deposit. The analysis found that average earnings currently fall £1,281 short of standard affordability requirements based on current rental levels.
